title: The server: what it loads and asks per request
grade_reasons: D stands, on the verified numbers. 559 of 562 pages, 181 of 268 route handlers and the proxy each load the same 10 to 12 MB of server code whatever their job (0.84 to 1.3 s to start cold on the review machine, against 0.16 to 0.24 s for the health check), every instance spends about 0.3 s in a start hook and 0.09 s reading a 10.4 MB list before its first request, and a product view sends about 18 statements where one answer changes. The one server-side check, the first byte of two warm pages, sees none of it. It is not an E, because nothing hurts a person before opening, and not a C, because the sound parts (82 of 85 cached reads tagged, a warm cached page that asks nothing, well-made admin lists) do not change what every function carries.
verdict_on_bar: Kept, after checking the floors. A lean route is 0.4 MB once the unused schema is out (/api/health is 1,155 KB, of which src/db is 599), and the simulated beacon ends at 0.96 MB, so 1.0 MB and 500 modules is a true bar. The store home's 4.0 MB stands (simulated 3.5 MB; Next's own code is 0.78 MB of it by m/chunks.md, not the 0.5 the steward wrote). The admin's 6.5 MB, the start hook's 60 files, the admin's statement counts, the cache lives and the zero rules per store domain stand. Tightened: (1) The proxy, 1.2 MB to 1.0 MB. It makes six small reads in front of every page, its simulated end is 0.8 MB, and it has no reason to be heavier than a beacon that writes. (2) A product view, 3 statements to 2. Stock is one statement (variantStockOf in src/server/catalog.ts); the steward's third was room for a minute poll that step 0.8 removes. One more only for a store with producer schemes, one more with price breaks. (3) 'A storefront page' was checked on the home alone, which step 2.4 turns into a static file. The pages that keep a function per view now have their own lines: product page, listing and search 4.6 MB and 1,700 modules; cart, checkout and account 5.0 MB and 1,800. On the review's own simulation they end at 1,930 to 1,996 module paths after every planned cut, against the home's 1,389. (4) All five beacons are named in the check; the steward's bar listed five and the plan checks one. (5) Admin prefetch at rest, 4 to 0: step 0.13's own check is already 0. (6) The orders list gets a number (9 or fewer in 2 waves) in place of '2 fewer than today'. (7) Requests through the proxy per page load get a target, 7, where the steward gave only today's 13 to 44. Loosened: (1) 'No admin text' on a store page becomes 'no registry and at most 16 catalogue files, about 0.15 MB': emails and alerts sent from shoppers' routes need their words, and that is step 2.25's own end figure. (2) 'Shown on Platform' for the routing-rule count is dropped; a build that fails above 1,600 of 2,048 holds it better. (3) Search stays at 10: its floor was never measured, so I did not invent one. Added: cold-load time against the health check for the proxy, a store page and an admin page, not only the beacon; production targets by kind of entry for step 1.16, which named one; at most 2 statements at an instance's start; a cold page that reads the same rows for 10 and for 500 products (the steward's first gap, now in the bar); no statement sent twice on the cart and checkout; and no scheduled job that refreshes a store's tag when nothing changed. Not measurable as written: (a) the beacon's 'within 100 ms of /api/health' needs the review's cold-load scripts, which step 0.1 does not move into the repo and step 1.8 does not run; (b) the manifest's load 'in production' cannot be timed from the start hook, because the step is inside Next; (c) statements were counted as commits (20 commits for 18 statements, idle floor 1), which cannot hold a bar of 2; (d) the route budget holds one sample route per kind, so a heavy product page passes behind a light home. Each is a shortfall below.

measures.name: Server code a cold function loads, by kind of entry
measures.today: By next analyze: /api/visit 1,890 modules and 10,475 KB; store home 2,419 and 11,944 KB; product page 2,516 and 12,289 KB; admin orders 2,349 and 12,068 KB; the proxy 9,729 KB of chunks; /api/health 308 and 1,155 KB, of which the unused schema is 599. One import cycle of 229 files is reached by 559 of 562 pages, 181 of 268 handlers and the proxy. 24 public handlers of 7 to 52 lines each load all of it. Cold load in a fresh process: 0.84 to 1.3 s for a fat entry, 0.16 to 0.24 s for /api/health.
measures.target_a: Each of the five beacons (the four /api/visit routes and /api/recommendations/events): 1.0 MB and 500 modules or fewer. The proxy: 1.0 MB of chunks and 120 source files or fewer, reaching none of auth.ts, pages.ts, catalog.ts, stores.ts, seo.ts, stripe.ts, admin-text.ts or sharp. Store home, built and blog pages: 4.0 MB and 1,500 modules. Product page, listing and search: 4.6 MB and 1,700 modules. Cart, checkout and account: 5.0 MB and 1,800. No store page loads the admin's text registry (at most 16 catalogue files), the AI tools, theme-store code or sharp, and only cart, checkout and account may load the order writer or the Stripe SDK. An admin list page: 6.5 MB, with only the text areas it draws and no AI engine before the assistant is opened. The largest import cycle in src/server: 19 files. Every handler over 1,500 modules is on a named list with its reason (181 today, about 29 expected), and the 24 small public handlers are under 800. Cold load, one run on one machine: a beacon and the proxy within 100 ms of /api/health, a store page within 300 ms, an admin page within 450 ms. No taxonomy file or image library is traced beside an entry that cannot use it.
measures.how_measured: src/server/route-load.graph.test.ts with its baseline on every pnpm test (source files reached per entry, forbidden modules, the largest cycle, the named list) and scripts/route-budget.mjs after the build in CI's e2e job (chunk bytes; today plus 4%, may only fall). Step 1.8 makes both. The budget must hold the largest route of each kind, not one sample. Module and MB figures: docs/audits/bloat-review-2026-11/scripts/server-graph.mjs over a next analyze export. The cold-load times need the review's cold-load scripts in the repo; no step puts them there (shortfall 3).

measures.name: What every instance pays before its first request
measures.today: Start hook: 383 source files, 856 modules and 2,383 KB of chunks; 0.27 to 0.34 s and 26 to 43 MB before the first request of every function, lean ones included. Then one statement, and one a minute per instance (278,393 runs in 78 days). The server-reference manifest: 10,397,955 bytes and 81,027 entries, 80 to 91 ms and 20 to 24 MB to load. Re-counted on the build: 547 admin routes hold 62,816 of the entries, 115 each at the median, and /api/visit lists 74 references it never calls. The unused schema: 56 to 114 ms and about 7 MB per copy, in 6 built files. All from the review machine; nothing times a cold start in production.
measures.target_a: Start hook: 60 source files or fewer and under 0.7 MB of chunks, with no ai.ts, auth.ts or admin text. At most 2 statements at start, and a poll at most every ten minutes, only where a translated language is served. Schema: 0 built files hold table definitions, and the graph test forbids the import. Manifest: under 5 MB and 40,000 entries, a median of 60 references or fewer for an admin route and 0 for a beacon; or a week of production readings that show its load under 30 ms at the median. In production, by kind of entry, the median time from process start to the first answer: a beacon and the proxy within 150 ms of the health check, a store page within 400 ms, an admin page within 600 ms, with cold starts a day shown beside them.
measures.how_measured: The graph test's baseline for src/instrumentation.ts (step 1.8) and step 0.8's unit test of startUi() for the 2 statements. scripts/route-budget.mjs prints the hook's chunk bytes and the manifest's bytes, entries and entries per route on every CI build; each may only fall. rg -l -F '.table("theme_schedules"' .next/server -g '*.js' prints nothing. Production: the instance.start line and the Platform page of step 1.16. That line cannot time a step inside Next as written (shortfall 4).

measures.name: Database statements per storefront view, warm
measures.today: An anonymous view of a prerendered product: about 18, 16 beyond the proxy's. Stock is the one answer that changes per view; it is one statement and it is sent twice. Search 11 to 12, with the search rules read twice. Category about 2. Home and a store's own page 0 of their own. A shopper with a cart: 2 identical cart counts per page. A signed-in shopper on a product page: 2 to 4 session reads. The cart page works its summary out twice, each time with 5 statements for features that are off. A cart with lines and the checkout were never counted.
measures.target_a: Product page: 2 or fewer beyond the proxy's, on the inventory tables only (one more for a store with producer schemes, one more for a store with price breaks). Category 2. Search 10 or fewer, with no settings table read twice and no store looked up by its id. Home and built pages 0. One cart count and one session read per request. A cart with three lines and the checkout: no statement sent twice with the same text and values, none for a feature the store has off, at most two waves after the shopper is known, and a count taken at the first run that may only fall.
measures.how_measured: scripts/server-budget.mjs in CI's e2e job (step 1.11), with each budget at its target and not above it. It must count statements, not commits: pg_stat_statements before and after one GET, or the counter of step 1.9. The shop-only journey of step 1.12 holds 'none for a feature that is off'. The cart with lines and the checkout enter with step 2.19.

measures.name: Function runs a store page view causes beyond its document
measures.today: /wishlist/saved on 12 of 12 store pages measured (twice on checkout), each also a proxy run. /api/shop/tiles with 3 statements on every page with a product grid, though both tile switches default to off. A render function on every view of 148 of 149 prerendered store routes: 97,919 of the demo home's 138,523 bytes are streamed per view to place two cart badges and a country hint. One Add to cart: 16 requests and 193 KB. 13 to 44 requests per page load pass the proxy. Crawlers on Next's bot list get a full render even of the 508 static pages.
measures.target_a: For a visitor with no cart, wishlist or account, on a store with tile stock off: 0 calls of the page's own after the document. Home, built, blog and info pages are 'static' in the prerender manifest and answer as cache hits (21 of the demo's 148 resuming routes), Kaizena Flow's front page among them. Product, listing, cart, checkout and account pages keep their one per-request part. At most 7 requests per page load pass the proxy on the home, a product page, a content page and the cart, and none for a page a press cannot open. One Add to cart: 1 request under 5 KB. A Bingbot request for a static page is a cache hit.
measures.how_measured: scripts/render-modes.mjs with scripts/render-modes.baseline.json after the build in CI (compute mode and holes per route; step 1.11). e2e/prefetch.spec.ts for the requests that pass the proxy (steps 0.12, 0.14 and 2.6). Assertions in e2e/wishlist.spec.ts, e2e/shop-components.spec.ts, e2e/search.spec.ts and e2e/cart.spec.ts. docs/audits/bloat-review-2026-11/scripts/measure-routes.mjs for the 12 store pages.

measures.name: What one save, poll or redraw costs in the admin
measures.today: Menu build: 125 ms of blocking CPU per store shell render (220 permission lookups for 110 paths; 243 ms for a closed store). At least 39 save sites draw the whole route twice, and 6 more are mixed. 51 to 66 KB of unchanged shell JSON is sent again per redraw. 8 progress polls redraw the whole route every 5 to 20 s, hidden tabs included. The notice poll: 4 statements, 60 times an hour per visible tab. 23 to 46 prefetch requests per screen.
measures.target_a: Menu: under 2 ms and 110 lookups per build. 0 saves that draw the route twice, the mixed ones included. Under 30 KB of shell JSON per redraw. No poll ticks in a hidden tab; a progress tick asks its job (2 or 3 statements), not the route; the notice poll asks 2 statements. 0 prefetch requests in the 3 s after a screen loads, and at most 2 after a hover.
measures.how_measured: The count test in src/lib/store-nav.test.ts (step 0.17). src/components/admin/router-refresh.scan.test.ts (step 0.18). e2e/signed-in/prefetch.spec.ts (step 0.13). e2e/signed-in/admin-scripts.spec.ts for the shell's bytes (step 2.28). src/server/assistant-notices.int.test.ts for the poll. The admin.render log line in production.

measures.name: What makes a cached store page draw again, and what a cold draw costs
measures.today: 71 of 85 cached reads expire after an hour, though 82 carry a tag that every write refreshes. Home and All products redraw every 15 minutes (6 routes). 319 of 1,316 prerendered entries carry the platform-wide tag ai-providers, which any one owner's save refreshes. One publish makes all 261 built pages of the demo store stale. Every deploy empties every cache (up to 52 deploys on 11 November). A cold store page makes an estimated 30 to 35 statements with about 5 waits in a row before its first byte. listPublishedPages() reads 29 whole pages a call: 79,778 calls and 781 s in 78 days. The front page reads every active product on each cold draw, and a product page's metadata loads the store's whole index; no finding counted either.
measures.target_a: 0 storefront routes at 15 minutes. A read whose every writer refreshes a tag lives a week; only reads with a clock in them (the 30-day reference price, campaigns, VAT labels) stay hourly. 0 store entries carry a tag that one store's action can refresh for another. A body-only publish makes that page's entries stale, not the store's. No scheduled job refreshes a store's tag when nothing changed. A cold store home: 20 statements or fewer, the instance's start included, and at most 3 waits in a row before the first byte; a cold home and product page read the same rows for a store of 10 and of 500 products. No caller reads every page to pick one. After each deploy the job, not a visitor, pays the first draw of Kaizena Flow's home and one store page, and a push that changes no app code deploys nothing.
measures.how_measured: scripts/render-modes.mjs baseline (revalidate seconds and tags that name no store, per route) and src/server/use-cache.scan.test.ts (both step 1.11). scripts/server-budget.mjs for the first request after a restart and for the 500-product store. src/server/query-budget.int.test.ts for the cold frame (step 1.10). The release job's log of page checks (step 0.3). The daily production reading of step 0.2 for the whole-pages statement. Nothing counts tag refreshes or page draws in production (shortfall 6).

measures.name: What a deployment carries per store
measures.today: 4 to 8 routing rules per store with its own domain, against Vercel's cap of 2,048 a deployment, of which the app's own routes take about 705: room for about 270 such stores. One full production deploy per domain change, which empties every cache. The list of store domains is parsed again 2 or 3 times for every link a page draws: at 1,000 stores with a domain about 64 ms per render of a page with 85 links.
measures.target_a: 0 routing rules and 0 deploys per store domain: .next/routes-manifest.json is the same with 0 or 300 active domains. 1 parse of the hosts list per instance. The count of routing rules is printed on every build, and the build fails above 1,600.
measures.how_measured: The new case in src/lib/store-hosts.test.ts (1,000 marketPath() calls parse once; step 0.20). scripts/route-budget.mjs counts the rules in .next/routes-manifest.json (step 1.8). CI's hosts job with a domain activated after the build (step 2.35).

bar_in_a_sentence: A function loads what its own job needs and little more: about 1 MB for a beacon and for the proxy, 4 to 5 MB for a store page, and a small, counted start for every instance. A page view asks the database only for what changes per view (stock on a product page, nothing on a home page), an admin screen shows its first content after one or two waves of reads, a cached page is drawn again only when something it shows has changed, and a test or a production figure holds each of these numbers.
can_the_steps_reach_a: No, not as written: they end at a strong B. Most values get there. Beacon: 10,475 KB to 1,173 (step 0.4) to 956 (2.22), under 1.0 MB by 4%. Proxy: 9,729 KB to about 2,400 (0.4, 0.6, 0.7) to about 800 (2.20). Store home: 11,944 KB to 7,700 (0.6) to 4,350 (0.4, 0.7) to 3,500 (0.6's two extra edges, 0.8). Admin orders: 12,068 KB to 8,200 (0.5, 0.4) to between 6.2 and 6.7 MB (2.25), thin against 6.5. Start hook: 383 files to about 50. Product view: 18 statements to 15 (0.22) to between 1 and 3 (2.13). Calls after the document: 1 or 2 to 0 (0.15). Requests through the proxy on the phone home: 47 to 23 (0.12) to 3 (2.6). Static store pages: 0 to 21 of 148 (2.4). Add to cart: 16 requests to 1. Store Home: 29 to 14 statements (2.32). Menu: 125 ms to 0.1 ms. Double draws: 39 to 0. Cold home: 30 to 35 statements to 20 (2.18). Four distances stay open. (1) The pages that keep a function per view: on the review's own simulation with every planned cut (work/sg-plan/after-5.json) the product page ends at 1,930 module paths and listing, search, cart and checkout at 1,995, against the home's 1,389 and a bar of 1,700 to 1,800. Short by 200 to 300 modules and about 1 MB each, and no step or check names them. I re-ran the cuts on the source graph: 837 to 910 files against the home's 531, because the cart's action file imports the order writer at its top. (2) The fifth beacon ends at 768 module paths against 500. (3) The manifest: the planned cuts take about 14%, to about 9 MB against 5 MB; step 2.24 acts only if production shows over 30 ms, cannot measure that as written, and is sized M for work that is an L. (4) Holds: the cold-load times have no script, the product budget is set at 4 against a floor of 1, the cart and checkout have no number, and nothing in production sees a job that refreshes a tag every run. Two measures also wait for the owner: measure 8 needs a yes to step 2.35, and without step 3.19 each push still empties every store's cache. With the seven additions below and those two answers the area is an A, and only after step 4.4, because the platform Home and the Payments page are held there.

shortfalls.what: The pages that run a function on every view are not in any check and do not reach the bar. Step 2.22 proves the store home only, and step 2.4 then makes the home a static file. After every planned cut the product page still reaches 1,930 module paths and listing, search, cart and checkout 1,995 (home 1,389; bar 1,700 to 1,800). Cause, read in the code: src/app/s/[store]/[market]/cart/actions.ts imports startCheckout and startExpress at its top, so every page with an Add to cart button loads the order writer, and with it draft orders, emails, staff alerts, billing and the books. product-parts.tsx imports express-checkout.ts, which imports checkout.ts and stripe.ts. The quote button's file imports the staff alerts, and through briefing, store-checkup and turnover-watch the ledger. store-part-section.tsx imports every working section, so a category page loads the order page's exchanges and returns.
shortfalls.proposed_step_title: Take the order writer off pages that only show products
shortfalls.proposed_step_what: Phase 2, effort L, after steps 2.9 and 2.22. Load checkout.ts, the alert and email senders and the Stripe SDK inside the action that uses them, as step 0.6 does for the home. Split express-checkout.ts into a facts file with no writer and the press. Let step 2.9's per-route section modules serve the server side too, with a server check. Those three cuts reach about 1,730 to 1,775 module paths by the source graph, so then follow the graph test's list of what the product page reaches beyond the home until the bar holds. Add the product page, a category, search, the cart and the checkout as entries of the graph test and of scripts/route-budget.mjs. The cuts are on order and payment paths: land them after step 0.3, one file's edges per commit, and place a test order after each deploy.
shortfalls.proposed_done_when: A next analyze export shows the product page, /category/[slug] and /search at or under 1,700 modules and 4.6 MB, and the cart, the checkout and the account at or under 1,800 and 5.0 MB (2,516 to 2,546 modules and 12.3 MB today). src/server/route-load.graph.test.ts shows the product page and a category reaching none of src/server/checkout.ts, stripe.ts, ledger.ts, staff-alerts.ts or billing.ts. The checkout, express checkout and quote specs pass.

Step 0.4 moves the helpers that come through chat-route.ts and does not name this import.

shortfalls.proposed_step_what: Effort S. In src/app/api/recommendations/events/route.ts import visitorKey from src/server/chat-turns.ts. Name the four /api/visit routes and /api/recommendations/events in the checks of steps 0.4 and 2.22 and as entries of the graph test of step 1.8.

shortfalls.proposed_step_what: Effort S. Copy the four cold-load scripts into docs/audits/bloat-review-2026-11/scripts/ with step 0.1. In scripts/route-budget.mjs load /api/health, /api/visit, the proxy, the start hook, the store home, the product page and the admin's orders page in fresh processes, five runs each, and hold each median's distance from /api/health's. It is 80 to 91 ms on the review machine, so that door will most likely stay shut, and the instance.start line cannot time a step that runs inside Next. The step is sized M, but its remedy is the reader and writer split the findings rate L. Step 0.19 has no statement count for the products list, so the baseline of step 1.9 would lock whatever it finds, not 5. Step 2.32 does not check the 2 statements after each shell render. Step 0.17 does not check that a progress tick asks its job, not the route. Step 0.18 leaves the 6 mixed saves uncounted. Step 1.16 gives one target (a beacon within 150 ms) for four kinds of entry. Step 1.8 prints the routing rules and fails on nothing. Step 0.13's check is 0 requests at rest while the steward's bar said 4.

shortfalls.what: Nothing in production sees why a cached page is drawn again. CI holds lifetimes and tags from the build, but a job that refreshes a store's tag on every run is invisible to it: the alt-text job did so 10 times in 10 runs and only this review found it. After step 2.15 gives reads a week's life, tag refreshes are the only thing that redraws a page, so an unseen one undoes the step.
shortfalls.proposed_step_title: Count tag refreshes and store page draws in production
shortfalls.proposed_step_what: Phase 1, effort S. In refreshTag() (src/server/refresh.ts) log one line per refresh through log(): the tag's family, the store's id, and whether an action, a job or a webhook called it. In the store layout log one line per draw with its statements, from the counter of step 1.9. Platform, Usage and limits shows refreshes and draws a day by family, and flags a store whose tag a job refreshed more than 10 times in a day. It holds measure 7 as a production figure.
shortfalls.proposed_done_when: The page lists a week of refreshes and draws by family, an int test sees the flag after 11 job refreshes of one store's tag, and a quiet day in production shows 0 job refreshes for stores where nothing changed.

shortfalls.what: The cart and the checkout, the path where money is taken, have a shape in the plan and no number. Step 2.19 asks for 'at most two waves' and step 1.11 counts only a home page with a cart cookie. Nothing fails when the same statement is sent twice in one request, which is how the cart came to work its summary out twice.
shortfalls.proposed_step_title: Give the cart and the checkout a count, and fail on a statement sent twice (add to steps 1.11 and 2.19)
shortfalls.proposed_step_what: Effort S. Let the counter of step 1.9 keep each statement's text and values. In step 1.11 count a cart with three lines and the checkout at its first step on the day the script is made, and write both numbers into docs/performance.md. In step 2.19 the budget becomes the count after its cuts, and the test fails when one request sends the same statement with the same values twice.
shortfalls.proposed_done_when: scripts/server-budget.mjs holds the cart with three lines and the checkout at their counted figures, each lower than the first count, in at most two waves; and a trial second call of cartSummary() in the cart page fails it.

tolerated: All four hand-written storefront languages load with every store page: 0.4 MB of its 4.0 MB. Loading one could show a shopper the wrong language. Look again when a fifth is added.
Every block's server code loads with the page renderer, about 1.8 MB of a store page, because one function serves every store's pages.
An admin page loads its own area's readers and writers together: about 2,000 modules and up to 6.5 MB. Splitting each area further is not worth it for a signed-in owner's first click.
Up to 16 files of admin words (about 0.15 MB) on shoppers' routes, for the emails and alerts those routes send.
The proxy runs once for every page request, and reads a store's facts once per store, instance and 10 seconds. That is what makes a private store private within seconds.
Stock is read from the database on every product view, one statement, by written rule.
Product, listing, cart, checkout and account pages keep a function per view. So does /themes, so its filter works without scripts.
The guard's two reads on every admin request. A security decision is never cached.
Two statements at every cold start for the interface texts, and about 30 KB of unchanged shell data per admin redraw.
A deploy empties every cache, because Next ties them to a deployment. The first view of each page after it is a full draw of at most 20 statements.
A cached, tagged read may fetch a row wider than it shows while the row is under about 10 KB.
A store's robots.txt, sitemap, llms.txt and feeds answer without a CDN cache: a crawler asks about once a day.
The taxonomy data and the image library stay in the package of functions that can use them. That is size on disk, not time.
owner_choices: May a store's own domain be looked up when the request arrives, replacing decision P8's routing rules compiled into each deployment (step 2.35)? Without a yes each store with a domain costs 4 to 8 of the host's 2,048 rules and a full deploy per change, the wall is near 270 such stores, and this area stops at a B.

Once stores are open, may a CI run skip its deploy when a newer commit is already on main, so a burst of pushes shares one (step 3.19)? Each deploy empties every store's cached pages and starts every function cold: up to 52 on 11 November. It changes D5's 'at once' by a few minutes. Without it the first visitor of each page after each push pays a full draw.
May the notice badge in a tab nobody touches be up to ten minutes late (step 2.34)? 60 requests an hour per open tab become 6. It shows at once on the next click.
Is a third admin language wanted in the first half year? If yes, step 2.25 moves before opening: until it is done each language adds about 1.5 MB to every admin function.
